contributorNote: Daasanach ('Af Dhaasanac / d’áasannæc / Dasanech / Dasenech / Galab / Geleba / Reshiat) Lowland East Cushitic (Western Omo-Tana / Galaboid) dictionary compiled manually and audited 100% line-by-line from Václav Blažek (2011) 'Dasanech Language – State-of-the-Art' (Folia Orientalia, Vol. 48, 2011, Masaryk University, Brno, reviewing Mauro Tosco 2001 'The Dhaasanac Language. Grammar, Texts, Vocabulary of a Cushitic Language of Ethiopia', Kuschitische Sprachstudien Band 17, Rüdiger Köppe Verlag, Köln, xiv + 598 pp. + 20 photos, ISBN 3-89645-064-6, and comparing Gabriele da Trento 1941 [60 units], Eike Haberland 1966 [91], Harold C. Fleming 1965 [102] & 1971 [146], M. Lionel Bender 1971 [97], Hans-Jürgen Sasse 1973–1982 [ca. 11 studies], and Mauro Tosco 2001 [c. 1,400 units] across 101 Swadesh glosses, 48 Abbreviations & 50 References), Sumiyo Nishiguchi (2004) 'Consonant Assimilation and Sonority : A Case Study in Daasanach' (OUPEL: Osaka University Papers in English Linguistics, Vol. 9, pp. 39–51, Osaka University Knowledge Archive [OUKA], DOI: 10.18910/70792 — fieldwork carried out in New York State from September 2004 to May 2005 with a native Daasanach speaker from Kenya; audited 100% line-by-line across Sections 1–5, Examples 1–34, Tableaux 1–4, Footnotes 1–9, and all 13 References), and Lieut. Ludwig von Höhnel (1894) 'Discovery of Lakes Rudolf and Stefanie' (Reshiat / Buma / Marle on the northeastern shore of Lake Turkana).

entries.english: 24 Consonant Phonemes, 5 Short/Long Vowels & 2 Diphthongs (ie, uo) in Dasanech (d’áasannæc)
entries.translation: Oral plosives: b, d, t, j, c, g, k, ʔ • Implosives: ɓ, ɗ, ʄ, ɠ • Nasals: m, n, ɲ, ŋ • Fricatives: f, ð, s, š • Trill: r • Approximants: w, y, l • Vowels: i, e, a, o, u (short & long) • Diphthongs: ie, uo

entries.english: Singulative & Plural Nominal Suffixes in Dasanech
